# Requirement #2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

plants.description: The null check on reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is dropped, so in the source generator context (where reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null) the lambda captures a null delegate and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation invokes it, throwing NullReferenceException and crashing the generator (CS8785).

The guard is changed from && to ||, so diagnostics that have no source location (metadata symbols) fall through to ContainsSyntaxTree(null), which throws ArgumentNullException and turns into an analyzer crash (AD0001) instead of dropping the diagnostic.

The metadata-safe lookup is reverted to direct indexing of DeclaringSyntaxReferences, which is empty for members of a closed generic type from a referenced assembly, so the original IndexOutOfRangeException crash returns and no resolver is generated.

The location filter is removed entirely, so the analyzer reports diagnostics for types and members that live in metadata or in another compilation; those diagnostics have no location in the analyzed compilation, which analyzers must not report.
Equivalent rewrite of the same check: IsInSource is exactly SourceTree is not null, so behaviour is unchanged.
Moves the cast to the syntax object instead of the as-expression; the resulting value and null behaviour are identical.

refused_to_decide: Whether the fix is complete: the issue reports that GetObjectInfo in TypeCollector.cs indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly at several locations (lines 735, 1009, 1101 in the issue's file version) in addition to the two locations shown in the diff. The diff does not show changes to those other locations, so it cannot be determined from the provided material whether all IndexOutOfRangeException crash sites for metadata symbols are eliminated or whether some remain.

variant_reviews.error: nemotron-3.5-super-vl gave an empty answer (finish_reason=length, 97302 characters of thinking). It probably spent the whole reply budget of 24000 tokens thinking; raise the budget.

findings.message: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation is a no-op: it unconditionally invokes report(diagnostic) without checking whether the diagnostic's location belongs to the current compilation. This defeats the method's stated purpose of filtering out diagnostics for types/members from referenced assemblies (metadata symbols). As a result, the analyzer will still report diagnostics for closed generic types defined in referenced assemblies, preventing a clean build and violating the principle that such diagnostics belong to the defining assembly.

refused_to_decide: The issue report identifies three locations in GetObjectInfo that index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101 in the referenced version). The diff only shows fixes at two locations. I cannot determine from the diff alone whether a third unaddressed direct index access remains on the code path for closed generic metadata types, which could still cause the IndexOutOfRangeException.

# Requirement #2283: Analyzer fails to report MsgPack004 for unkeyed members of a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

`MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` does not report `MsgPack004` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly** and that referenced type has a public member without a `[Key]` attribute. The consuming project builds without any diagnostic, but the unkeyed member is silently ignored during serialization, causing data loss at runtime. In our case, `Item<int>.Unkeyed` was dropped from every `Cmd` payload across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key)
{
    public int Unkeyed { get; init; }
}
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A build that reports `MsgPack004` in `app` for `Item<int>.Unkeyed`, pointing at the `Member` property in `Cmd` (or at the `Item<int>` usage), so the consuming project knows the referenced type is not fully serializable. The generator should still produce a resolver in `app`.

#### Actual behavior

```
Build succeeded.
    0 Warning(s)
    0 Error(s)
```

`app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`, but serializing `Cmd` omits `Item<int>.Unkeyed`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` with unkeyed member | **no diagnostic** |
| `struct Item<T>` with unkeyed member | **no diagnostic** |
| `struct Item` with unkeyed member | ok (MsgPack004 reported) |
| `record struct Item` with unkeyed member | ok (MsgPack004 reported) |
| `class Item<T>` with unkeyed member | ok (MsgPack004 reported) |
| `record class Item<T>` with unkeyed member | ok (MsgPack004 reported) |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the diagnostic appear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

**Stack trace.** None; the analyzer completes without reporting.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type suppresses the need for the diagnostic, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

findings.message: The change wraps reportDiagnostic with ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which suppresses all diagnostics whose location is outside the current compilation. As a result, MsgPack004 for unkeyed members of closed generic value types from referenced assemblies is not reported in the consuming project. The requirement explicitly expects the diagnostic in app so the consuming project knows the referenced type is not fully serializable. The documentation changes (README.md lines 1641-1642, doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md lines 49-52) confirm the intended behavior is to report in the defining assembly instead, which does not satisfy the requirement.
